title: Access to guns a factor in fatal standoff, inquiry told
article: A flimsy plywood cabinet where a gunman got his arsenal the day he shot at his mother and a friend should never have been approved by police, a firearms official told a coroner's jury Tuesday.
On the last day of testimony in the inquest into David Melzer's shooting death, Det. Sgt. Lynn Pretty said the gun vault in the Melzer home didn't meet accepted standards.
"If I had gone to Mr. Melzer's home I wouldn't have approved that gun vault," she said.
The 33-year-old man was killed by police June 2, 2000, after an 11-hour standoff and shootout at his parents' home.
Pretty also said the man's father, John Melzer, should have had to move his guns out of the house when police learned his son was banned from guns.
A judge imposed the ban in 1996 following a 6 1/2-hour standoff in 1995 with Stratford police.
